name: Discord Bridge
description: Bidirectional text bridge between your Meshtastic mesh and a Discord channel. Mesh traffic is relayed into Discord; Discord messages are transmitted over the air.

discord_token.description: Bot token from the Discord Developer Portal (Bot -> Reset Token)

discord_channel_id.description: Target channel ID, digits only. Stored as a string because snowflakes exceed JavaScript's safe integer range

discord_to_mesh.description: Relay Discord messages onto the mesh

mesh_channel_index.description: Meshtastic channel index used for transmissions

mesh_channel_filter.description: Which mesh channel to listen on: 'all' or a channel index

forward_dms.description: Also relay direct messages addressed to your node

relay_web_chat.description: Mirror messages composed in the MeshPulse web chat into Discord. MeshPulse transmits those itself and notifies no plugin, so they are detected by watching its message store rather than through a hook

web_chat_poll_seconds.description: How often to check the MeshPulse message store for newly sent messages

web_chat_label.description: Name shown in Discord for messages composed in the MeshPulse web chat

name_prefix.description: Prefix outbound messages with the Discord author's display name

dm_target.description: Optional node ID (!xxxxxxxx). When set, every Discord message is sent as a direct message to this node instead of a broadcast

thread_per_node.description: Open a Discord thread for every node automatically. Off by default: mesh traffic arrives in one channel, which is what a single operator watching their own mesh wants. Threads opened by hand with the 'open' command keep working either way

thread_scope.description: Which mesh traffic opens a thread: 'all' = every sender, 'dm' = only direct messages (broadcasts stay in the main channel)

thread_archive_hours.description: Hours of silence before Discord archives a thread. Archived threads are reopened automatically on the next message

thread_name_template.description: Thread title. {name} = node name, {id} = node ID

pairing_enabled.description: Let Discord users claim a mesh node by transmitting a one-time code from it

pair_code_ttl_minutes.description: How long a pairing code stays valid

pair_require_dm.description: Require the code to arrive as a direct message. On firmware 2.5+ that is encrypted to this node, so the code cannot be stolen off the air. Turn off only for legacy radios

greet_new_members.description: DM a pairing code to anyone who joins the server. Needs the SERVER MEMBERS INTENT in the Discord developer portal

paired_role_name.description: Optional Discord role granted once a node is paired. Leave empty to skip. The bot needs 'Manage Roles'

simulate_enabled.description: Enable the 'simulate' command, which injects a fake mesh packet for testing without a second radio. Anyone in the channel can forge traffic while this is on - keep it off in normal use

use_embed.description: Render inbound mesh messages as embeds instead of plain text

allow_bots.description: Relay messages from other bots and webhooks. Enable with care: it removes a loop guard

max_payload.description: Maximum encoded size of a single text packet, in bytes

max_chunks.description: Maximum number of packets a single long message may be split into

tx_interval.description: Delay between consecutive transmissions, in seconds. Protects the duty cycle

echo_ttl.description: Window for detecting the bridge's own messages coming back over the air, in seconds

log_to_db.description: Persist bridged messages to the plugin's SQLite database
